runTokenAuth.description: A run-scoped token issued when a worker claims a task run. It carries neither a user session nor access to any store a user route reads.

checks.description: Every dependency probed. An empty array means nothing was verified.

name.description: Which dependency, never where it lives

sandboxed.description: False means nothing confined the run's Bash commands

sources.description: Layer chain that decided the boundary, e.g. default:worker, settings, policy

path.description: The call's file_path argument, when it had one

run_id.description: Agent run id; also the trace file's name

tools_truncated.description: The tools list was bounded; tool_calls still counts them all

error.description: Terminal error; empty when the run succeeded

complete.description: False means the run wrote no terminal record — do not read as success

Invitation.description: A pending offer of team membership against an account that already exists. Never carries a code -- see docs/design/team-membership-lifecycle.md.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency token; PATCH must send the version it read

RunIssue.description: The bounded view of an issue a run's agent reads. Not the full issue: children are title and status only, and the comment thread is a recent window.

omitted_comments.description: How many older comments the window left out

author_kind.description: "agent" is a run this deployment scheduled and recorded. "local_agent" is an agent on someone's own machine, reported over their session — a claim, not something the deployment observed.

author_id.description: A user_id, or an agent_id for "agent". For "local_agent" it is the person who reported it

post.summary: Create a secret with its items

patch.summary: Edit a secret's items (whole-map replace, or set/remove patch)

409.description: Error

put.summary: Change a secret's state (active, disabled, destroyed)

get.description: Reports that the process is running. Checks no dependencies by design — a liveness probe that failed on a dependency outage would restart a healthy server.

Reports whether the server can serve traffic, probing each configured dependency. Names the failing check but never the reason, which goes to the server log: this endpoint is unauthenticated and connection errors carry DSNs and endpoints.

post.description: Accepts either a `password` (the everyday credential) or a single-use `otp` login code (the recovery path, issued by an operator). Returns an access token and, when the deployment stores them, a refresh token. `token` repeats `access_token` under the name it had before the two were split.

post.summary: Set or change the caller's password
post.description: Requires the current password when the account already has one: a session by itself must not be enough, since an access token cannot be revoked before it expires. Setting the first password after signing in with a login code needs no current password.

400.description: New password fails the length rule, or body invalid

401.description: Not authenticated, or the current password is wrong

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new token pair
post.description: Unauthenticated: possession of the refresh token is the proof. Each exchange spends the token presented and returns its replacement in the same session. Presenting a spent token past `refresh_rotation_grace` revokes the whole session.

401.description: Token unknown, expired, revoked, or reused

503.description: Deployment has no refresh token store

post.description: Accepts either credential: a refresh_token in the body names its session, otherwise the session comes from the access token's sid claim. Revoking a session the server has already forgotten is a success.

503.description: Deployment has no refresh token store

get.summary: List the caller's own pending invitations, across every team
get.description: Not team-scoped: it answers what is pending for the signed-in caller. See docs/design/team-membership-lifecycle.md.

post.description: Takes no code: the caller already reached this session on their own, so this is authorized by the invitation being their own pending row, not by proving anything a second time.

404.description: Not found -- covers an invitation belonging to someone else, the same as one that does not exist

409.description: Already accepted or revoked, or expired

get.summary: List the models this deployment offers for managed inference
get.description: Being signed in is the whole authorization: the catalog is deployment-global, so every enabled model is available to every user. Identity is resolved before the gateway is touched, so an unauthenticated caller learns nothing about whether this deployment offers managed inference.

post.summary: Run one managed model call, so a client needs no upstream provider credential
post.description: Names a model from the deployment catalog; upstream endpoints, credentials, and provider model identifiers are never accepted or returned. Unknown request fields are rejected rather than ignored. With stream=true the response is text/event-stream carrying delta, result, and error events. A foreground call is attributed to the caller and metered against no team.

200.description: OK. A streamed call that fails after its first delta still answers 200 and reports the failure as an error event

400.description: Invalid request, unknown field, or a model that is not in the catalog or is disabled

409.description: This call_id has already been used

post.summary: Run one managed model call on behalf of a task run, so a worker needs no upstream provider credential. Authenticated with the run token the scheduler minted for that run: user, team, task, and run all come from the credential, never from the request

200.description: OK. Same body and streaming behaviour as the user route

400.description: Invalid request, unknown field, or a model the run's team may not use

401.description: Missing, invalid, or expired run token

403.description: The run token authorizes a different task run, or a different team than the run's

409.description: The run is not executing, so no call is accepted for it

post.description: Authenticated with Authorization: Bearer <webhook key> or X-Webhook-Key.

post.summary: Create a team-owned task and its initial run
Continue a task with a new input

409.description: Run already in progress

post.description: A run that has not been dispatched is canceled outright and answers 200. A run a worker already holds is asked to stop and answers 202; it reaches CANCELED when that worker confirms, or when the server's backstop finishes it.

202.description: Cancel requested; the run's worker is stopping it

409.description: No run in progress, or it already finished

post.summary: Run the task's last run again
post.description: Creates a new run with the same input as the task's most recent finished run, recording which run it repeats. Takes no body. A task whose run is still in flight, one that has never finished a run, and one belonging to a workflow step all answer 409.

409.description: A run is in progress, there is no finished run to retry, or the task belongs to a workflow step

get.summary: List artifact files for a task run
Get a task run's trace summary
get.description: What the run used, touched, spent, why it ended, and the execution boundary it ran under. Model output, tool arguments, and tool results are deliberately excluded.

404.description: The run recorded no trace, or its trace is no longer in storage

get.summary: List a task run's managed model calls
get.description: What the run spent and on which approved alias, oldest first. An accounting record, not a transcript: prompts, tool arguments, and generated content are absent, and so is the catalog entry the alias resolved to, which is the operator's routing rather than the team's.

200.description: OK. An empty array when the run made no managed calls, which is what a direct-mode run does

404.description: No such run for this team

503.description: This deployment records no managed calls

post.summary: Issue a login code for a locked-out member of the caller's own team
post.description: Owner only. Does not replace the system_admin route in system-administration.md, which still recovers an owner who has no co-owner and no admin left in their own team -- this only removes the dependency on a system_admin existing at all for the common case of one member locked out of an otherwise healthy team. See docs/design/team-membership-lifecycle.md.
